indicator_rows.name: Hardcoded Secrets & Credentials
indicator_rows.reason: clean tree; 1 history-only finding(s) — per SEC-02 Yellow flag: rotated secrets in history — score 2.

pointers.detail: git log -p --all over bounded history; history_scanned_full=true

remediation.quick_win: rotate EVERY leaked credential immediately (the exposure window starts at commit time, not discovery time), remove from current tree, switch to env vars.
remediation.structural: adopt a secret manager + injection (Vault, Secrets Manager), ban secrets in code via CI scanners on every commit *and* a history scrub, least-privilege per environment, kill the "secrets in docs" habit.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero secrets in the tree or history; secrets injected at runtime from a manager; CI blocks secret commits; rotation drill run annually.

remediation.structural: fuzz-in-CI for parser-adjacent code, migrate memory-unsafe parsers, input-validation as a platform concern, adversarial corpus maintenance.
remediation.gold_standard: Every untrusted parser fuzzed in CI with sanitizers, zero standing crashes, validation layers reject early and clearly.

indicator_rows.name: Security Testing in CI
indicator_rows.reason: No security CI jobs — classes none; jobs none — per SEC-10 Red: no SAST/deps/secret/image gates — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: add Semgrep/CodeQL failing gates, secret scan on history + CI, TRIVY on images — this week.
remediation.structural: a security-as-quality pipeline (SAST, deps, secrets, container, DAST on staging, threat modelling for new features), a findings tracking loop (owner, SLA, retest), and a hard "no gate-less merge" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Five scan categories failing in CI, findings tracked to closure within SLA, DAST regularly scheduled, threat modelling on all new boundaries.

remediation.gold_standard: Core framework within 1 major of current; < 30% of direct deps behind by a major; automatic update PRs flowing weekly; majors scheduled explicitly on the roadmap.

indicator_rows.name: Missing Runbooks & Operational Docs

remediation.quick_win: write runbooks for the top 5 incident classes today (postmortem-driven), make them linkable from alert dashboards, add "runme at the first sign" steps.
remediation.structural: runbook-as-product (owned, tested, games rehearsed), alert→runbook binding, postmortem = runbook update, drill the top runbook quarterly.
remediation.gold_standard: Every incident class has a current, tested runbook; on-call executes procedures not improv; incident time is dominated by execution, not discovery.

indicator_rows.name: No Onboarding Guide / Developer Setup Docs
indicator_rows.reason: No onboarding guide — no CONTRIBUTING.md / GETTING_STARTED.md and README has no setup section; stages missing: setup, run, test — per DOCS-04 Red flag: no documentation, new hires rely on tribal knowledge — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: write the golden path (clone → setup → run → test → first PR) and verify every command executes, add CONTRIBUTING.md.
remediation.structural: golden path CI-verified (fresh container proves it — DOCS-09), onboarding checklist wired into the ticket system, "setup docs break" = blame-the-repo not the human.
remediation.gold_standard: A new hire takes < 2 hours to a working local env entirely from docs; the setup guide is CI-tested and always current.

indicator_rows.name: No Release Communication / Changelog
indicator_rows.reason: No CHANGELOG.md found at any of 6 candidate paths; 0% of 0 sampled releases carry notes — per DOCS-08 Red flag: breaking changes ship unannounced, consumers learn from failures — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: adopt a CHANGELOG process (Keep-a-Changelog, auto-generated from commits/PRs), publish release notes for the top consumers, write migration guides for open breaking changes (backfill).
remediation.structural: semantic-release automation (version + changelog + notes automated), a release-communication channel (port status page + email), "breaking = migration guide in same MR" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Every release has automated notes; every breaking change has a migration guide published with the change; consumers hear first, break never (silently).

indicator_rows.name: Docs-as-Code & Automation
indicator_rows.reason: No docs-as-code automation — zero CI steps; no link-check; no API generation — per DOCS-09 Red flag: docs are wiki-only, drift unverified — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: wire docs generation into CI (spec → reference), add links/lint checks for markdown, CI-verify the top setup commands (fresh container).
remediation.structural: full docs-as-code — generate what's generatable, verify what's actionable, staleness gates (docs touch-required on code change), docs failures block merge like code failures.
remediation.gold_standard: Docs build like code, generate from truth, verify their own commands, and fail CI on rot — the knowledge layer is as maintained as the code.

full_table.name: Runtime/Language EOL
full_table.reason: java@1.7 (cycle 7, EOL PASSED, pin pom.xml); EOL runtime confined outside core — per ECOS-01 Yellow flag: EOL in an isolated path — score 1.

remediation.quick_win: document the gap, create the upgrade ticket with a date.
remediation.structural: parallel runtime upgrade plan — run new runtime in CI behind a feature gate, migrate one service at a time, dual-run in prod. For truly stuck runtimes, isolate behind a facade and treat like a rewrite candidate.
remediation.gold_standard: Every production runtime within its vendor-supported window; CI builds a canary job on the current runtime; a deprecation calendar exists and is reviewed quarterly.

full_table.name: Major Package Drift
full_table.reason: 33.3% ≥1 major behind, 33.3% ≥2; worst core gap org.apache.struts:struts2-core 4 major(s) — per ECOS-02 Red flag: core framework stuck ≥2 majors — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: enable Dependabot/Renovate with major-update grouping and a monthly budget.
remediation.structural: "upgrade train" — pick one major hop per quarter, keep intermediate commits shippable, use the dependency graph from tools to sequence hops (don't skip majors). Establish a "never more than 1 major behind" policy for core deps.
remediation.gold_standard: Core framework within 1 major of current; < 30% of direct deps behind by a major; automatic update PRs flowing weekly; majors scheduled explicitly on the roadmap.

full_table.name: Missing Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)
full_table.reason: No decision records — no ADR directory found; architecture changes are undocumented — per DOCS-01 Red flag: decisions live only in heads, onboarding requires a listening tour — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: write ADRs for the top 10 load-bearing decisions (interview the oldest engineers, mine git/past docs), establish a template + PR requirement for consequential choices.
remediation.structural: ADR convention in the repo (ADR-NNN, status, decision, context, alternatives considered), decisions now documented at review time, an "explain every load-bearing choice" refactoring task.
remediation.gold_standard: Every consequential decision has an ADR with alternatives; new decisions document as standard practice; teams can revisit a decision on evidence, not memory.

full_table.name: Missing Runbooks & Operational Docs
full_table.reason: No runbooks — searched searched docs/runbooks, runbooks, docs/operations etc.; zero files found — per DOCS-03 Red flag: incidents recovered by heroics, every lesson repeated — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: write runbooks for the top 5 incident classes today (postmortem-driven), make them linkable from alert dashboards, add "runme at the first sign" steps.
remediation.structural: runbook-as-product (owned, tested, games rehearsed), alert→runbook binding, postmortem = runbook update, drill the top runbook quarterly.
remediation.gold_standard: Every incident class has a current, tested runbook; on-call executes procedures not improv; incident time is dominated by execution, not discovery.

full_table.name: No Onboarding Guide / Developer Setup Docs
full_table.reason: No onboarding guide — no CONTRIBUTING.md / GETTING_STARTED.md and README has no setup section; stages missing: setup, run, test — per DOCS-04 Red flag: no documentation, new hires rely on tribal knowledge — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: write the golden path (clone → setup → run → test → first PR) and verify every command executes, add CONTRIBUTING.md.
remediation.structural: golden path CI-verified (fresh container proves it — DOCS-09), onboarding checklist wired into the ticket system, "setup docs break" = blame-the-repo not the human.
remediation.gold_standard: A new hire takes < 2 hours to a working local env entirely from docs; the setup guide is CI-tested and always current.

full_table.name: No Release Communication / Changelog
full_table.reason: No CHANGELOG.md found at any of 6 candidate paths; 0% of 0 sampled releases carry notes — per DOCS-08 Red flag: breaking changes ship unannounced, consumers learn from failures — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: adopt a CHANGELOG process (Keep-a-Changelog, auto-generated from commits/PRs), publish release notes for the top consumers, write migration guides for open breaking changes (backfill).
remediation.structural: semantic-release automation (version + changelog + notes automated), a release-communication channel (port status page + email), "breaking = migration guide in same MR" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Every release has automated notes; every breaking change has a migration guide published with the change; consumers hear first, break never (silently).

full_table.name: Docs-as-Code & Automation
full_table.reason: No docs-as-code automation — zero CI steps; no link-check; no API generation — per DOCS-09 Red flag: docs are wiki-only, drift unverified — score 0.

remediation.quick_win: wire docs generation into CI (spec → reference), add links/lint checks for markdown, CI-verify the top setup commands (fresh container).
remediation.structural: full docs-as-code — generate what's generatable, verify what's actionable, staleness gates (docs touch-required on code change), docs failures block merge like code failures.
remediation.gold_standard: Docs build like code, generate from truth, verify their own commands, and fail CI on rot — the knowledge layer is as maintained as the code.

steps.name: Skipped / Disabled Tests
steps.quick_win: re-enable or delete each skip deliberately (delete-with-justification or fix-with-test); no skips without a linked ticket and owner.

steps.name: Major Package Drift
steps.quick_win: enable Dependabot/Renovate with major-update grouping and a monthly budget.

steps.name: Build Reproducibility & Lockfile Integrity
steps.quick_win: commit the lockfile, switch CI to `npm ci`/`pip install --require-hashes`/`--frozen-lockfile`, add a "lockfile up-to-date" CI check.

steps.name: Hardcoded Secrets & Credentials
steps.quick_win: rotate EVERY leaked credential immediately (the exposure window starts at commit time, not discovery time), remove from current tree, switch to env vars.

steps.name: No Onboarding Guide / Developer Setup Docs
steps.quick_win: write the golden path (clone → setup → run → test → first PR) and verify every command executes, add CONTRIBUTING.md.

steps.name: Runtime/Language EOL
steps.quick_win: document the gap, create the upgrade ticket with a date.

steps.name: Missing Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)
steps.quick_win: write ADRs for the top 10 load-bearing decisions (interview the oldest engineers, mine git/past docs), establish a template + PR requirement for consequential choices.

steps.name: Missing Runbooks & Operational Docs
steps.quick_win: write runbooks for the top 5 incident classes today (postmortem-driven), make them linkable from alert dashboards, add "runme at the first sign" steps.

steps.name: No Release Communication / Changelog
steps.quick_win: adopt a CHANGELOG process (Keep-a-Changelog, auto-generated from commits/PRs), publish release notes for the top consumers, write migration guides for open breaking changes (backfill).

steps.name: License Compliance Risk
steps.quick_win: generate an SBOM (`syft . > sbom.json`), wire it into CI, publish attribution files.

steps.name: Input Robustness & Fuzzing
steps.quick_win: stand up fuzz harnesses for the top 3 untrusted parsers, run sanitizer builds, harden validation at those boundaries (limits, types, structure).

steps.name: Security Testing in CI
steps.quick_win: add Semgrep/CodeQL failing gates, secret scan on history + CI, TRIVY on images — this week.

steps.name: Docs-as-Code & Automation
steps.quick_win: wire docs generation into CI (spec → reference), add links/lint checks for markdown, CI-verify the top setup commands (fresh container).
